title: Auditor number decline continues
full_text:
The number of SMSF auditors has continued to decline at a steady rate, falling for the third year in a row, with the total around 30 per cent lower than five years ago, according to data released by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC).
In the “ASIC Annual Report 2025-26” released yesterday, the regulator noted the number of auditors under its oversight at the end of the 2026 financial year was 3596, a decline of nearly 300 from the 3882 recorded at the end of 2024/25.
This decrease follows a similar trend over previous financial years where auditor numbers fell by 280 from the 4162 recorded at the end of 2023/24, which was preceded by a drop of 261 from 4423 at the end of the 2023 financial year.
The most significant decrease in the past five years was the decline in practitioner numbers of 750 across the 2023 financial year from 5173 at the end of 2021/22.
Collectively, from 2021/22 to 2025/26, the number of SMSF auditors declined by 1577, or by around 30 per cent, and follows a slow fall off in numbers since 2014 when ASIC first reported that 7073 practitioners were registered with the regulator.
The annual report did not provide specific data on the replacement rate for SMSF auditors, but rather bundled them in with registered company auditors and authorised audit companies, stating that collectively only 185 applications of all types were approved while another 39 were refused or withdrawn.
Despite the downward trend, the regulator has commented it is not concerned with ASIC enforcement inquiries, with compliance senior executive leader Peter Ridgley earlier this year stating it was in part due to a change where it no longer viewed registered company auditors as SMSF auditors, as well as the exit of practitioners no longer working with SMSFs.
During the 2026 financial year, ASIC acted against 64 auditors, removing the ability for more than two-thirds of them to practice.
In previous statements, the regulator said between 1 July 2025 and 31 December 2025 it had disqualified four SMSF auditors and cancelled the registrations of 22 practitioners, and in the second half of the financial year had cancelled 21 registrations.
Many of the cancellations were related to breaches of professional obligations, such as failing to maintain independence, failing to lodge annual statements, failing to keep up to date with professional development requirements and practical experience, and non-compliance with auditing and assurance standards.
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation and Investments
